claims.text: A widget's build returns new child widget objects each time it runs; Flutter then rebuilds each child whose new widget is not the same instance as the previous one, down the subtree, without checking whether the data changed.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/best-practices.md ('traversal to rebuild all descendents stops when the same instance ... is re-encountered'); resources/inside-flutter.md

claims.text: Every evaluation of a const widget expression yields the one same object, so a parent's rebuild hands Flutter the same instance and the subtree is skipped (its build, e.g. a print in it, does not run) unless the widget has a change of its own, such as a provider it watches.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/best-practices.md ('const constructors ... short-circuit most of the rebuild work'); ui/adaptive-responsive/best-practices.md ('Flutter can reuse const widget instances')

claims.text: In Riverpod, a ConsumerWidget whose build calls ref.watch on a provider runs build again when that provider's value changes; widgets that did not watch it are not rebuilt by the change, and ref.read does not watch.

At stage-2, ProductListScreen.build calls _actions(context, ref), which calls ref.watch(authProvider) to choose the sign-in or sign-out IconButton; ProductCatalog is created inside build's data builder.
At stage-2, signing out therefore reran ProductListScreen.build, created a new ProductCatalog instance and rebuilt the catalog and its tiles, though only one icon changed.

claims.text: A widget marked for rebuild by its own watched value rebuilds even when its parent passes the same instance; the same-instance shortcut applies only to a widget that is not dirty.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: resources/inside-flutter.md ('if an element has not marked itself as dirty, the element can return immediately ... identical widget')

claims.text: A helper method called from build runs as part of that build, so a ref.watch inside it makes the whole widget rebuild when the provider changes.
claims.source_hint: riverpod.dev/docs: Ref.watch (the WidgetRef belongs to the widget whose build received it); stage-2 _actions

claims.text: Calling setState rebuilds that State's widget and its descendants, so it should be called as low in the tree as the part that changes.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/best-practices.md ('When setState() is called on a State object, all descendent widgets rebuild ... localize the setState() call')

claims.text: When only part of a screen depends on a provider, watch it in that part (a separate widget) rather than in the screen's build.
claims.source_hint: refs/flutter-website: perf/best-practices.md (split large build functions by how they change); outline items 3-4
